Development build. Network isolation and unattended reliability still need verification before security use.
Setup and testing
1. Prepare the devices
Use Android 10 or later. Install the APK on each camera. Put cameras and viewers on your private network. Reserve each phone’s IP in your router. Do not forward camera ports to the internet.
2. Create identities on your computer

From the Lantern project folder, run the commands below. Replace the sample address with this phone’s real address. Create the household CA once; create a different peer identity for every camera. Commands prompt for passwords.

python3 scripts/provision.py init-ca --out provisioning/household-ca\n\npython3 scripts/provision.py create-peer --ca provisioning/household-ca --out provisioning/front-door --name \"Front door\" --san 192.168.1.20

Keep household-ca/ca-key.pem offline. Transfer only front-door/device.p12 to this camera. Import it using its export password. Delete the transfer copy afterward. Add a Meshnet name with another --san when you are ready to test that route.
3. Trust the camera on each viewer

Install only the public household-ca/ca-cert.pem as a trusted CA on each viewer. On iPhone/iPad, also enable full trust under Settings, General, About, Certificate Trust Settings. Browser and TV trust stores differ. Never bypass warnings.
4. Finish the phone setup

Follow the 5 setup steps. Allow camera and microphone access. Start the camera. Copy a reachable certificate address into your viewer’s browser. Generate a pairing code, enter the camera address and viewer name in the browser, pair, then select Watch. Confirm real live video before finishing.
5. Test video, sound and snapshots

Move in front of the camera and confirm the image changes. Take a snapshot, reopen history and download it. Connect with audio and select Listen. Select Talk, allow the viewer microphone and test sound in both directions. Stop Talk and check the microphone indicator turns off. Use headphones or separate rooms to limit feedback.
6. Test privacy and recovery

Pair a second viewer. Revoke its access in Camera settings and confirm it loses video and snapshot access. Pause the camera: live media stops but saved snapshots remain available. Stop the connection: the viewer goes offline. Start locally again. Repeat after screen-off, network changes and reboot on both Samsung and MIUI.
7. Qualify the network and hardware

Test actual S23 Plus, Redmi, iOS, Windows and TV devices. Inspect selected WebRTC routes on LAN and Meshnet. Configure router/OS restrictions for HTTPS 8443, discovery UDP 8444 and negotiated media ports, including IPv6. Test unauthorized off-network reachability and 24-hour wired operation. The app does not enforce a firewall or prove isolation.
Detailed desktop walkthrough: docs/setup-and-test.md in the project. The hardware acceptance checklist is docs/device-acceptance.md.
